editorial_contributions.text: It has been conjectured by \textit{P. Erdős} [Math. Mag. 52, 67--70 (1979; Zbl 0407.10001)] that the only powers of \(2\) which do not have the digit \(2\) in their ternary expansions are \(2^n\) with \(n=0,2,8\), but only some upper bounds for the number of such \(n\leq x\) are known. The author considers a similar question for sequences \(y_n(\lambda)=\lambda2^n\) and \(x_n(\lambda)=[\lambda2^n]\) for positive \(\lambda\). For real or integral \(3\)-adic number \(a\) denote by \((a)_3\) the sequence of its ternary digits. It is shown first (Th.1.1) that the number of \(n\leq X\) such that in \((x_n(\lambda))_3\) the number \(2\) does not occur is \(\leq 25X^{0.9725}\) for large \(X\), and (Th.1.2) there exists an infinite sequence \(n_k\) such that for uncountably many \(\lambda\)'s \((x_{n_k}(\lambda))_3\) does not contain \(2\). Then the author proves (Th.1.3) that the set of \(\lambda\)'s such that \((x_n(\lambda))_3\) omits \(2\) is of Hausdorff dimension \(\log_3(2)\) and conjectures that Hausdorff dimension of the analogous set for the sequence \(y_n\) equals zero. He shows also (Th.1.5) that if \(\lambda\) is a non-zero \(3\)-adic integer, then the number of \(n\leq X\) such that \((\lambda2^n)_3\) omits \(2\) is bounded by \(2X^c\), where \(c=\log_32\). The next theorem brings an approximation to the analogue of Theorem 1.3 in the \(3\)-adic case. Finally intersections of multiplicative translates of Cantor sets in the \(3\)-adic case are discussed.

Let \(1<k<33/29\). In the paper under review, using the Davenport-Heilbronn version of the circle method, the authors prove that if \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_3\) are non-zero real numbers, not all of the same sign and that \(\lambda_1/ \lambda_2\) is irrational and \(\varpi\) is any real number, then for any \(\varepsilon>0\), the inequality 
\[
 |\lambda_1p_1+\lambda_2p_2^2+\lambda_3p_3^k+\varpi|\leq (\text{max}_jp_j)^{-(33-29k)/(72k)+\varepsilon} 
\]
 has infinitely many solutions in prime variables \(p_1, p_2, p_3\).

\[
 \int_X^{2X}\left(\theta((x+h)^{1/k})-\theta(x^{1/k})-((x+h)^{1/k}-x^{1/k})\right)^2dx, 
\]
 which plays a key role in the proof of the main result of this paper.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Erdős conjectured that 1, 4, and 256 are the only powers of two whose ternary representations consist solely of \texttt{0}s and \texttt{1}s. Sloane conjectured that, except for \(\{2^0, 2^1, 2^2, 2^3, 2^4, 2^{15}\}\), every other power of two has at least one 0 in its ternary representation. In this paper, numerical results are given in strong support of these conjectures. In particular, we verify both conjectures for all \(2^n\) with \(n \leq 2 \cdot 3^{45} \approx 5.9 \times 10^{21}\). Our approach makes use of a simple recursive construction of numbers \(2^n\) having prescribed patterns in their trailing ternary digits.

editorial_contributions.text:
The paper deals with the problem of determining the rank of powers of quadrics, namely, given a non-degenerate \(n\)-ary quadric, which can always be written as \(q_n = x_1^2+ \ldots + x_n^2\), one wants to know the (Waring) rank of \(q_n^s\), i.e. the minimum number \(r = rk(q_n^s)\) of linear forms such that we have \(q_n^s = l_1^{2d} + \ldots + l_r^{2d}\). When considering the space \({\mathbb P}^N\) parameterizing \(n-ary\) forms of degree \(2s\), this means that we can find \(r\) distinct points \(P_1,\ldots,P_r\) on \(V_{n,2s}\), the \(2s\)-Veronese embedding of \({\mathbb P}^{n-1}\), such that the point \(T=[q_n^s]\), which parameterizes \(q_n^s\), is such that \(T \in <P_1,\ldots,P_r>\). A different notion of rank is the one of \textit{border rank}: a form \(f\in S^{2s}\mathbb C^n\), parameterized by a point \(T\in {\mathbb P}^N\) has border rank \(brk(f) = r\) if there is 0-dimensional subscheme \(X \subset V_{n,2s}\) of length \(r\) such that \(T \in <X>\). So, of course, we have \(brk(f) \leq rk(f)\).

The main result in the paper is the computation of \(brk(g^s)\) for every power of a ternary quadric \(g \in S^{2s}\mathbb C^3\); namely, one gets 
\[
brk(g^s) = rk(g^s) =\binom{s+rh(g) -1}{s-1},
\]
if \(g\) is degenerate, while, if \(g\) is non-degenerate, 
\[
brk(g^s) =\binom{s+2}{2}.
\]
The main tools for this results are the determination of the apolar ideal of \(q_n^s\) (which is of interest \textit{per se}), that turns out to be the space of harmonic polynomials, and border apolarity, a result by W. Buczynska and J. Buczynsky, which allows to work on border rank in a similar way as the classical apolarity is used for the rank.

editorial_contributions.text:
The paper studies representations of large integers in the form 
\[ 
[u^c]+[v^c]+ [w^c]
\] 
in nonnegative integers \(u,v\) and \(w\) for a number \(c\) in a given interval (\([x]\) denotes the integer part of the number \(x\)). The paper proves, that if \(c\) is a fixed number in the interval \((1; \frac{7}{4})\), then any sufficiently large integer may be represented in the above mentioned form. The paper studies also some cases when one of the three variables is restricted to a sparse subset of positive integers.

editorial_contributions.text:
In the classical Waring-Goldbach problem one studies the representability of integers as sum of powers of primes. The study of the arithmetical properties of \(p+2\) for primes \(p\) is related to the famous twin prime conjecture. In the present paper, the authors study an interesting hybrid variation of both problems. They prove that for \(1<c<2173/1930=1.1259\cdots\) and \(N\) sufficiently large, the Diophantine equation 
\[
\lfloor p_1^c\rfloor+\lfloor p_2^c\rfloor+\lfloor p_3^c\rfloor=N
\]
is solvable in prime variables \(p_1\), \(p_2\), \(p_3\) such that each of \(p_1+2\), \(p_2+2\), \(p_3+2\) has at most 
\[
\lfloor 11387/(4346-3860c)\rfloor
\]
prime factors, counted with multiplicity. This improves on a result of \textit{Z. Petrov} [God. Sofiĭ. Univ., Fak. Mat. Inform. 104, 171--183 (2017; Zbl 1474.11171)] who had the smaller range \(1<c<17/16=1.0625\). The proof uses Rosser's sieve and exponential sum techniques (exponent pairs). The paper is very well written, contains a nice historical overview on the problem and an extensive bibliography.

title.title: On a ternary Diophantine equation involving fractional powers with prime variables of a special form

editorial_contributions.text: Let \(p\) be a fixed odd prime and \(Q(x, y, z) = ax^2 + bxy + cy^2 + dxz + eyz + fz^2\) be a fixed quadratic form with integer coefficients which is non-degenerate modulo \(p\) and satisfies the extra condition \((a(4ac-b^2), p) = 1\). The author studies the asymptotic behavior of solutions of the congruences \(Q(x,y,z)\equiv 0 \bmod{p}^n\) in small cubes, where \(n\) tends to infinity. He obtains an asymptotic formula for a suitably smoothed counting function if the side lengths of the cubes exceed \(p^{n/2+\varepsilon}\). His method uses an explicit \(p\)-adic parametrization of the solutions, the Poisson summation formula and an evaluation of exponential sums with rational functions modulo \(p^n\).
